title: Closed-fibre quotient of the tensor kernel vanishes
statement: Let the local rings, local maps, tensor product D, map F, flatness, surjectivity, and kernel equality be as in lem-weil-pbc-finite-coefficient-tensor-kernel-reduction. Writing K = ker F and L = m_A D, every x ∈ K maps to zero in the quotient D/(L K).

proof.text: Use the proved closed-fibre calculation to obtain ker F⊆m_A D.

Equip D with its right A-algebra structure and B with φ.toAlgebra. The tensor formula makes F A-linear. Use the proved Mathlib theorem LinearMap.ker_inf_smul_top_eq_smul_of_flat (Mathlib.RingTheory.Smooth.Quotient), with hsurj and hflat, to get ker F∩m_A D=m_A ker F. Since every kernel element lies in m_A D, it lies in m_A ker F. Ideal.smul_top_eq_map and Ideal.smul_restrictScalars identify these A-submodules with the D-ideal notation. Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero finishes. This uses Mathlib directly instead of the planned flat-quotient-tensor-injective node.

proof_origin.place: Remark 07NS (4), closed-fibre isomorphism; Proposition 07NQ, kernel-tensor paragraph. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NS and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NQ.
